subject.title: [Bug]: Cron agent jobs silently time out during sustained LLM API outages instead of fast-failing on definitive errors

question: For plain provider messages like `LLM error api_error: Internal server error`, should OpenClaw treat them as cron-local provider-outage `server_error`, shared provider cooldown signals, or timeout-only failures, and when should failure delivery notify?
rationale: The choice affects fallback timing, shared auth-profile health, scheduler retry semantics, and user-visible failure notifications, so automation cannot safely pick the default policy from source inspection alone.

options.title: Cron-local provider outage
options.body: Classify the cron-visible failure as retryable `server_error`, prove early fallback abort/advance, and avoid shared auth-profile cooldown unless the provider signal is structured enough.

options.title: Shared provider cooldown
options.body: Treat plain internal-server API failures as provider outage signals that can skip same-provider candidates across jobs, accepting broader cooldown effects for faster recovery.

options.title: Timeout-only with proof
options.body: Keep plain provider 500 text as timeout-like only if focused cron/fallback tests prove the run no longer burns the outer deadline and failure alerts are adequate.

recommendation.title: Cron-local provider outage
recommendation.body: Classify the cron-visible failure as retryable `server_error`, prove early fallback abort/advance, and avoid shared auth-profile cooldown unless the provider signal is structured enough.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest recent mix of prior policy review and adjacent cron/runtime history for this cross-surface product decision.
